title: Telemetry ingest
summary: How one Sparkplug packet becomes stored readings. The top row shows what happens when a packet or a birth does not fit. The second row runs inside the MQTT callback and the third is the durable part.

boxes.label: MQTT message
boxes.detail: The runtime subscribes to NBIRTH, NDATA, NDEATH, DBIRTH, DDATA and DDEATH for each connection's group, with ordered delivery.

boxes.label: packet()
boxes.detail: Parses the topic and drops anything outside the connection's group. Any packet marks its source as heard for offline detection, before validation. A running capture records the raw sample here.

boxes.label: Match devices
boxes.detail: Finds active device definitions bound to this connection, edge node and device ID. A birth is also reported to Laravel as a discovery event; it never creates a trusted device. Each device is handled under its own lock and skipped if its configuration or generation changed meanwhile.

boxes.label: Compatibility check
boxes.detail: Previews the source's current birth metrics against the applied configuration. A birth that matches again clears an earlier review.

boxes.label: Map to readings
boxes.detail: For each mapped metric: pick the observed time (source or receipt), apply the ingress conversion, validate against the parameter, then run profile calculations. A reading that fails is kept with a quality other than good.

boxes.label: Durable handoff
boxes.detail: Publishes the readings with the applied generation and session to the IOT_DEVICE_TELEMETRY stream, deduplicated by message ID. If the publish fails the device's presence becomes unknown, because a data gap may exist.

boxes.label: devices-storage
boxes.detail: One message in flight, explicit acknowledgement. A message for a configuration or generation that is no longer applied is discarded, not stored.

boxes.label: One transaction
boxes.detail: Good readings become observations; others become diagnostics and keep the last valid value visible. The same transaction writes latest values, the committed-telemetry outbox row and the hour's data point usage. A redelivered message and a re-sent buffered sample add nothing.

boxes.label: Committed relay
boxes.detail: Publishes outbox rows in order and acknowledges each before the next. On failure it backs off up to 30 seconds and retries the same event.

boxes.label: Automations, app streams
boxes.detail: The automation evaluator and the integration API's telemetry stream read only committed telemetry. The portal does not stream; it polls.

boxes.label: Rebirth request
boxes.sub: NCMD, at most 1 per 30 s per edge node
boxes.detail: A rejected packet marks presence unknown for what it broke and asks the edge node for fresh births. Requests inside the 30-second window are queued. Duplicates are dropped silently.

boxes.label: Review required
boxes.detail: The source's birth no longer fits the applied configuration. The device stays online with a diagnostic, its readings stop, and a person reviews and activates a configuration.

steps.text: A device publishes DDATA. The broker delivers it to the runtime's subscription for that connection's group.
The topic is parsed and the group checked. The source is marked as heard, then the packet goes to the Sparkplug engine.
If there is no session, a sequence gap, an unknown alias or a changed datatype, the packet is rejected and the runtime asks the edge node for a rebirth.
An accepted packet comes back with its session and decoded metrics. The runtime finds the active devices bound to this source.
For each device, the source's current birth is checked against the applied configuration.
If the birth no longer fits, the device is marked review required and nothing is mapped.
Otherwise metrics become readings: conversion, validation, then calculations. Invalid readings keep the last valid value visible but marked.
The readings are published to JetStream with the applied generation. From here the MQTT callback is done.
The storage consumer takes one message at a time and discards any whose configuration is no longer applied.
One transaction writes observations or diagnostics, latest values, the outbox row and usage.
The relay publishes the outbox row to the committed stream.
Automations and integration applications' streams see the reading only now, after it is stored.
